title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. J = {0,1,∞} (written 3 in the transcription). Π_J is a combinatorial fundamental groupoid of P^1 − {0,1,∞}, built from an S_3 × {1,τ}-equivariant cell decomposition. Here τ is complex conjugation. The vertices are P_i^ω and R_i^ω (ω = ±), placed near the punctures, and three real points Q_i. The Q_i are fixed by τ; they are 'midpoints' of the three real intervals, e.g. 1/2, 2, −1. The arcs are the half-loops a_i^ω around puncture i, the arcs b_i^ω, and the arcs c_i^ω: Q_i → R. S_3 permutes the arcs c_i^ω simply transitively. The local groups π_1 at the vertices are identified with a fixed π_{0,3} via the maps φ_i^ω and ψ_i^ω. On π_{0,3} act the involutions σ_∞, ε_0, τ_0 and an order-3 rotation ρ (the previous page has ε_0σ_∞ = ρ^{-1}).

Problem. Describe the automorphisms u of the profinite groupoid Π̂_J that fix the vertices, commute with 𝔖_J, and stabilise the local subgroupoids Π̂_{J,i} generated by P_i^± and a_i^±. These are the 'inertia-preserving' automorphisms, i.e. the candidate image of Gal(Q̄/Q).

Step 1, the local data. One has u(a_i^ω) = a_i^ω φ_i^ω(l_0^γ). Here γ = (p−1)/2 ∈ Ẑ and p ∈ Ẑ* is the cyclotomic-type exponent. Since a is a half-loop, a 'half-power' γ appears, with p = 2γ+1 (cf. next page). A NB remarks that one need not assume a priori that the local factor λ ∈ π̂_{0,3} is a power of l_0.

Step 2, the global datum. One has u(c_i^ω) = c_i^ω ψ_i^ω(η), with a single η ∈ π̂_{0,3} independent of (i, ω). This is the action on the path from the puncture-adjacent vertex to the real midpoint Q_i. The previous page has b = c c'^{-1}. It follows that u(b_i^ω) = b_i^ω φ(β) with β = σ_∞(η)η^{-1}.

Step 3, the relations. Relations (12) of earlier pages are now written in β and p. The first relation, β σ_∞(β) = 1, is automatic from (23): σ_∞(η)η^{-1} · η σ_∞(η)^{-1} = 1. This is the 2-cycle relation f(x,y)f(y,x) = 1. The remaining relation is (24): α ρ^{-1}(α) ρ^{-2}(α) = 1, with α = l_0^γ β (in general σ_∞(λ)β). This is exactly Drinfeld's hexagon relation f(z,x)z^m f(y,z)y^m f(x,y)x^m = 1 with m = (p−1)/2.

Step 4, moving the base point to the midpoints Q_i. Formula (25) gives u(ã_i^ω) in terms of α̃ = η^{-1} l_0^γ ε_0(η), in general η^{-1}ε_0(λη). Formula (25 bis) gives α = ρ(η α̃ ρ^{-1}(η)^{-1}).

Step 5, the symmetries of (24). Equation (24) is invariant under α ↦ ρ^{-1}(α) and under the twisted conjugation α ↦ x α ρ^{-1}(x)^{-1}. In other words, (24) is the norm (1-cocycle) condition for Z/3 = ⟨ρ⟩ acting on π̂_{0,3}, and the twisted conjugation is a change by a coboundary. By the invariance under twisted conjugation, (24) for α is equivalent to the analogous equation (26) for α̃.

The next page then shows that inertia-preserving automorphisms of the three-vertex groupoid Π^{III}_J ⟺ solutions α̃ of (26). That groupoid has vertices Q_i, six arcs ã and relations (16). The page also singles out (boxed) the special form α̃ = y^{-1} l_0^γ ε_0(y): α̃ is ε_0-twisted-conjugate to l_0^γ, the form coming from Galois via the path η. In that case the local monodromy becomes y^{-1} l_0^p y.

So the page is a derivation of the GT-type defining relations (2-cycle and hexagon) of the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group, from an equivariant groupoid model of P^1 − {0,1,∞}. The associator is parametrised as a coboundary σ_∞(η)η^{-1} of the 'half-path to the midpoint', and the hexagon is read as a Z/3 cocycle condition.
errors: Notational clash risk: the transcription reads the cyclotomic exponent as ρ (γ=(ρ−1)/2, ρ∈Ẑ*), but the image has p. The letter ρ is reserved for the order-3 automorphism of π_{0,3} in (24) and (25 bis). The next page confirms p = 2γ+1.

Gap: writing u(c_i^ω) = c_i^ω ψ(η) with a single η makes the 2-cycle relation automatic. But a general inertia-preserving automorphism of the profinite groupoid need not a priori have β of coboundary form σ_∞(η)η^{-1}. The page assumes this parametrisation rather than proving it. The left-margin NB on the ambiguity η ↦ η·(something) addresses only the non-uniqueness of η.

Claimed invariance of (24) under α ↦ xαρ^{-1}(x)^{-1}: this is correct (the product becomes x·1·x^{-1}, using ρ^3 = 1). Invariance under α ↦ ρ^{-1}(α) is also correct (conjugation by α^{-1}). No error here; just note that ρ must be an honest automorphism of order 3.
The underbrace 'σ_∞(λ)' under l_0^γ in (24) implicitly uses that in the special case σ_∞ fixes the local factor as written, or that one is in the general-λ version. This is not justified on the page.

ideas.what: Inertia-preserving, S_3-equivariant automorphisms of the profinite fundamental groupoid of P^1−{0,1,∞}, with half-loops at the punctures giving the local factor l^{(p−1)/2}.
ideas.modern_name: Profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT^ (Drinfeld 1990, Ihara), with half-power m=(λ−1)/2.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990); Ihara (1990s); program in Grothendieck's Esquisse (1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) describes the program qualitatively, without these explicit relations.

ideas.what: Derivation of the 2-cycle and hexagon relations for the action, with the hexagon as α ρ^{-1}(α) ρ^{-2}(α) = 1, α = l_0^γ β.
ideas.modern_name: GT relations (I) and (II): f(x,y)f(y,x)=1 and f(z,x)z^m f(y,z)y^m f(x,y)x^m = 1.

ideas.what: Parametrisation of the associator as a coboundary β = σ_∞(η)η^{-1}, where η is the action on the path from a puncture-adjacent base point to the real midpoint Q_i. This makes the 2-cycle relation automatic.
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition of f_σ through the base point 1/2 (half-path / 'f = g(y,x)^{-1}g(x,y)'-type decomposition).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in Galois–GT literature (Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps); exact credit unsure

ideas.what: Hexagon relation as a 1-cocycle (norm) condition for Z/3 acting by the rotation ρ, invariant under twisted conjugation α ↦ xαρ^{-1}(x)^{-1}. Hence a change of base point to the midpoints gives an equivalent equation in α̃.
ideas.modern_name: Non-abelian H^1(Z/3, π̂_{0,3}) / twisted-conjugacy formulation of the hexagon.

ideas.what: Reformulation of GT on the three-vertex 'triangle' groupoid with base points at the real midpoints Q_i (arcs ã, relations ã ã ã = 1). Distinguished Galois-type solutions α̃ = y^{-1} l_0^γ ε_0(y) are ε_0-twisted-conjugate to l_0^γ.
ideas.modern_name: GT via tangential/real base points on the three real intervals; 'dessin' triangle groupoid.

missed.claim: Grothendieck isolates the special class of hexagon solutions with α̃ ε_0-twisted-conjugate to l_0^γ, i.e. α̃ = y^{-1} l_0^γ ε_0(y). This is automatically true for Galois elements. Implicitly it raises the question whether every solution of (26) (every inertia-preserving equivariant automorphism) is of this form, i.e. whether the relevant twisted non-abelian cohomology class is forced. The question is not settled here.
missed.quote: α̃=η^{-1}ε_0(λη), valable quel que soit λ … (27) α̃ = y^{-1} l_0^γ ε_0(y)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives a cohomological criterion distinguishing Galois-type elements of GT^. It is related to the open question of whether Gal(Q̄/Q) → GT^ is surjective. I am not aware of this twisted-conjugacy criterion being studied as such.

missed.claim: The hexagon relation is presented as a Z/3 norm/cocycle condition and the 2-cycle relation as a Z/2 coboundary condition, both on π̂_{0,3} with the S_3 action. GT data thus becomes non-abelian cohomology of the S_3 × Z/2 symmetry of P^1−{0,1,∞}, with base-point changes acting as coboundaries.
missed.quote: invariante par substitutions α↦ρ^{-1}(α) … et α↦xαρ^{-1}(x)^{-1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A clean equivariant-cohomological packaging of GT relations. It is not the standard presentation in the GT literature and might simplify the profinite 2-cycle issues, e.g. whether the 2-cycle relation forces a coboundary decomposition.

missed.claim: An explicit derivation of Drinfeld-type 2-cycle and hexagon relations (with the half-power m = (p−1)/2) for the Galois/inertia-preserving action on π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}), predating Drinfeld 1990.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority. It is broadly suspected from the Esquisse, but the explicit relations in an equivariant groupoid formulation are not in print under Grothendieck's name.

deep.surprise_reason: The page explicitly derives the GT^ hexagon and 2-cycle relations, which specialists will find historically notable but not unexpected given the Esquisse and Schneps' archival work. The less standard features are the coboundary parametrisation β = σ_∞(η)η^{-1}, the twisted-conjugacy (Z/3-cocycle) reading, and the midpoint-groupoid reformulation with Galois-type solutions singled out. These are modest additions.
transcription_corrections: 'γ = (ρ−1)/2, ρ∈Ẑ*' should read 'γ = (p−1)/2 ∈ Ẑ, p ∈ Ẑ*' (cf. next page p = 2γ+1); likewise 'en β, ρ (ou γ)' should be 'β, p (ou γ)'.

The first lines read approximately: 'On prend un automorphisme u des groupoïdes Π̂_J qui commute à 𝔖_J et qui fixe les sommets, et qui conserve plus ou moins bien stables les sous-groupoïdes Π̂_{J,i} (i∈J)'. 'conserve Σ̂_3' should be 'commute à 𝔖_J', and the index 3 is J.
'Π_{J,i} engendré par les sommets P_i^ω (ω∈ω) et les deux flèches a_i^ω' — the reading 'deux sommets' is doubtful; the image has 'les/sommets'.
'L'automorphisme u est connu quand on connaît les u(a_i^ω), qui sont de la forme' — fine. The line before it, 'Alors', is struck out.
'savoir (B)' is probably 'à savoir (12)', a reference to relations (12) of the earlier page; uncertain.
Left-margin NB: approximately 'NB Si on remplace η par η·(…), alors β est remplacé par …τ_0(β)'; uncertain reading.
In (25) the subscript/superscript is ψ_{ω* i}^{ω*} on the left side and ψ_{ω' i}^{ω'} on the right.
